title: Lower bound on high-degree vertices in a k-chromatic graph
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph whose chromatic number equals $k$. Then $G$ has at least $k$ vertices of degree at least $k-1$; that is, the number of vertices $v$ with $\deg_G(v) \ge k-1$ is at least $k$.
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
the chromatic number of G equals k
replaced:
\emph{Every \texttt{k}-chromatic graph has at least \texttt{k} vertices of
degree at least \texttt{k - 1}.}
